decisions.reason: A addresses B as 'sir' in turn 5, which is a well-grounded inference of male gender in standard usage.
decisions.counterexample: In rare contexts 'sir' could be used as a generic polite honorific regardless of gender.

decisions.reason: A's references to 'They will be ready' and 'all the clothes when they are cleaned' presuppose B has clothes currently being washed/cleaned.

decisions.claim: B's clothes will be ready by 7:00
decisions.reason: A explicitly states 'They will be ready by 7:00' referring to B's clothes.

decisions.claim: B's clothes will be pressed when cleaned
decisions.reason: A explicitly states 'We will press all the clothes when they are cleaned' referring to B's clothes.

decisions.claim: B has items (clothes) that need washing/cleaning
decisions.reason: c5 ('B has items/clothes that need washing/cleaning') is bidirectionally equivalent to c2 ('B has clothes/items being washed') at the same granularity.

decisions.claim: B requested that clothes be pressed/ironed
decisions.reason: A says 'We will press all the clothes' as a service offer/commitment. There is no evidence B specifically requested pressing; A may have volunteered this service. B could have simply said 'yes please' or not asked at all.
decisions.counterexample: B only asked for washing and A proactively offered pressing as part of the standard service.

decisions.reason: c7 ('B is addressed as sir') is the evidential basis already captured by c1; both refer to the same fact from the same quote at equivalent granularity.

decisions.claim: B expects clothes to be ready by 7:00
decisions.reason: A states 'They will be ready by 7:00' as a commitment/information. There is no evidence B specifically expects or anticipated this time; B may not have been present when the time was discussed or may not care about the exact time.
decisions.counterexample: B simply asked for washing and A volunteered the 7:00 timeline without B expressing any expectation about it.

decisions.claim: B has multiple clothes/items (more than one piece)
decisions.reason: A uses 'all the clothes' (plural with definite article), which presupposes multiple items of clothing belonging to B.

design: dual route, targeted rescue, globally grouped evidence adjudication
